title: Automating Financial Calculation Validation
business: A fintech startup building a microservices-based interest calculation engine.
problem: Manual verification of interest logic is slow and error-prone, leading to inconsistent financial reporting across services.
solution: Implementing Jest as a centralized test runner allows developers to define deterministic unit tests for core calculation functions, ensuring consistent output before deployment.
steps: Install Jest as a development dependency using npm or yarn.
Define core logic in a standalone module, such as interestCalculator.js.
Create a corresponding test file, interestCalculator.test.js, using the test() and expect() functions.
Update the package.json scripts section to include a test command that invokes the Jest runner.
Execute the test suite via the command line to validate logic against expected outcomes.
outcome: Developers gain immediate feedback on logic changes, significantly reducing the risk of regressions in financial calculations.
limitation: Jest does not perform type-checking when using Babel for TypeScript transpilation; developers must run the TypeScript compiler separately to ensure type safety.
